sections.html: Appleton is the seat of Outagamie County, on the Fox River about 30 miles southwest of Green Bay. The 2020 census counted 75,644 residents in 24.82 square miles. Most of the city lies in Outagamie County, with smaller pieces in Calumet and Winnebago counties, and the city sits in five school districts. That split affects you in two ways: the Assessor keeps more than one tax rate and assessment level, and delinquent tax goes to a different county treasurer depending on where your parcel falls.

sections.h2: Who assesses and who bills property tax in Appleton?
sections.html:
The city handles both jobs, split between two offices. County involvement begins only after a bill is delinquent.

  • Assessor's Office, (920) 832-5850. Values every parcel, keeps ownership and lot descriptions, and mails a notice when an assessment changes. Revaluation of all property happens at least every five years, and the aim is an inspection of each parcel at least every ten.
  • Finance Department, (920) 832-6442. Bills and collects tax at City Hall, 100 N. Appleton St. On weekdays you can pay at the first-floor desk or the drive-up window, use the night deposit box, mail a check to P.O. Box 2519, Appleton, WI 54912-2519, or pay online through the Payment Center. Paying online adds a processor fee, and none of it goes to the city.
  • City Clerk, (920) 832-6443. Takes notices of intent to object and objection forms for the Board of Review.

The Finance page on the city website carries a copy of your bill and a breakdown of where the money goes. Your tax is the net rate per $1,000 times your assessed value. The rate comes from the combined budgets of the school district, city, county, sewer district, technical college and state reforestation.

Appleton splits the bill into four installments, due January 31, then March 31, May 31 and July 31, and each date is printed on the statement. State law has bills out by the third Monday in December. If any installment is late, the installment option is cancelled and monthly interest runs from February 1 on the unpaid balance. The interest rate under Wis. Stat. 74.47 is one percent a month, and a county board can tack on up to half a percent monthly as a penalty.

Once a balance is delinquent, the city stops collecting it. The county treasurer takes over unpaid balances from 2025 and earlier, and which county that is depends on the parcel.

Refunds work like this. If you pay in person with an escrow check and are owed $750 or less, you may get the refund in cash. Larger refunds, and any refund on a mailed or drop-box payment, are mailed within four to six weeks. An escrow check payable to the owner and the City of Appleton must be endorsed by both.

sections.h2: How the Appleton assessment and appeal process works
sections.html:
Each spring the city mails a Notice of Changed Assessment, then holds an informal Open Book review ahead of the formal Board of Review. Once the board meets, that year's assessments are final. Ask the Assessor for the calendar for the coming year. The law sets the notice lead time at 15 days before the board meets, stretching to 30 days when the city revalues.

To object, follow the steps the Clerk lists:

  • Start with a conversation with the Assessor, which the Clerk lists as step one.
  • Give the City Clerk notice of intent, spoken or written, no later than 48 hours before the Board of Review first convenes.
  • Hand in Objection Form PA-115A during the first two hours of that first session.
  • Bring evidence. The Board presumes the assessor got it right, so proof is the owner's job.

The board has seven members: the Mayor, the City Clerk, three alderpersons and three residents. A decision can go to circuit court by certiorari within 90 days of the notice of decision under Wis. Stat. 70.47.

By the time the December bill arrives, it is too late to object. Paying under protest is not an objection unless you first appealed to the Board of Review.

sections.h2: Which credits reduce an Appleton tax bill?
sections.html:
The bill can show two state credits. If you lived in the house as your primary residence on January 1 of the levy year, the lottery and gaming credit is yours, and the dollar amount moves from year to year. The first dollar credit is applied automatically to every taxable parcel with an improvement on it, whether or not the owner lives there. For the lottery credit, contact the treasurer of your county.

What you do to the house can also move the assessment. Routine work such as a new furnace, roof repair, gutters or patched walls generally does not raise it, though several items together might. Additions, finished basements, new decks and extensive kitchen or bath remodels usually do. Assessors visit recently sold homes in the fall and winter, so expect a letter after a sale.

sections.h2: What fees apply when I sell an Appleton house?
sections.html:
On a sale, the seller covers the state's 30 cents per $100 of value, a charge written into Wis. Stat. 77.22. Collection happens when the deed is recorded, after both parties sign an electronic transfer return. Whether Outagamie, Calumet or Winnebago County does the recording depends on where the parcel sits.

Wis. Stat. 77.25 exempts certain conveyances from the fee. A deed claiming an exemption has to state its reason right on the document. Examples include transfers by will, descent or survivorship, foreclosure transfers and deeds in lieu to the mortgage holder, sales for delinquent taxes, and transfers between parent and child or grandparent and grandchild for little or no payment. A regular sale to an unrelated buyer does not qualify.

sections.h2: Clearing unpaid Appleton property tax before a sale
sections.html:
Have the title or escrow company order a payoff from the correct treasurer. For the current bill that is the Finance Department. For 2025 and earlier years it is the county treasurer, and the payoff includes interest from February 1. A delinquent real property tax is wiped out by paying the balance, with interest and any penalty, ahead of the date a tax certificate is issued on the parcel.

Do not wait for the bill if a closing will fall near a deadline. Let the closing agent know which installments you have already paid. For an inherited or long-held house with a fuzzy tax history, phone the Finance Department with the parcel number. That call shows quickly what is open.

The tax side of an Appleton sale follows a short sequence.

  • Find your parcel number and note which county it sits in.
  • Ask Finance at (920) 832-6442 which installments are paid on the current bill.
  • If any earlier year is open, call the county treasurer from the table above for a payoff with interest.
  • Check whether an assessment notice arrived recently, and if you plan to object, remember the Board of Review calendar.
  • Hand the payoff letters to the closing agent, who will settle the balances from your proceeds.

Appleton's three-county layout is the detail most likely to trip up a seller, so write down your county early. A parcel on the Calumet side sends delinquent tax to a different office, and recording happens in that county as well. Sellers in the Winnebago corner, a small slice of the city, should be especially careful because most Appleton guidance assumes Outagamie County.

Selling to a cash buyer can speed things up since no lender is underwriting, though the transfer return, recording and tax payoff are still required.

faqs.q: When are Appleton property taxes due?
faqs.a: Four deadlines: the last day of January, March, May and July. A missed one ends the installment plan and starts interest running from February 1. Payment options are City Hall, mail, the drop box and the online center.

faqs.q: Which county treasurer do I pay if my Appleton taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Whichever county treasurer covers the parcel's location: Outagamie at (920) 832-5065, Calumet at (920) 849-1457 or Winnebago at (920) 232-3420. The city sends unpaid balances for 2025 and earlier years there.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Appleton assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at (920) 832-5850 first. Next, notify the City Clerk of your intent at least 48 hours before the board's first meeting, and turn in Objection Form PA-115A in that meeting's first two hours.

faqs.q: Seller's transfer fee in Appleton: how does it work?
faqs.a: The seller does. The Register of Deeds takes 30 cents per $100 of value when the deed is recorded. Transfers by inheritance, foreclosure deeds and some family conveyances are exempt.

faqs.q: Can I pay property tax under protest instead of appealing?
faqs.a: No. Paying under protest is not an objection unless you first filed an appeal with the Board of Review. The objection has to happen in spring, before the December bill arrives.
